    • isRecord

      public boolean isRecord()
      A Java record, which is the one kind of class that extends java.lang.Record: the language allows no other, and the compiler recognises a record the same way. Scala has no records, so this is only ever true of a class read from the classpath.
      Specified by:
      isRecord in interface io.micronaut.inject.ast.ClassElement

    • isAssignable

      public boolean isAssignable(String type)
      Whether this element is assignable to the named type.

      A type name carries no array dimensions -- an element for Array[String] is named java.lang.String and reports one dimension separately -- so this used to answer for the component type and call Array[String] assignable to String, and Array[Array[String]] assignable to Array[String]. Micronaut matches bean types, @Requires conditions and executable handlers through this method, so an array bean satisfied an injection point for its component type. An array is assignable by name only to the three types every array really is.

      Specified by:
      isAssignable in interface io.micronaut.inject.ast.ClassElement

    • isAssignable

      public boolean isAssignable(io.micronaut.inject.ast.ClassElement type)
      Whether this element is assignable to the given element, which unlike a name can be an array. Core's default delegates to isAssignable(String), which discards the dimensions of both sides.
      Specified by:

    • getCanonicalName

      public String getCanonicalName()
      The source-level name of the type, with nested types separated by a dot.

      Core's default returns Element.getName(), which is the binary name -- nest.Outer$Inner. The Java module answers with the qualified name, nest.Outer.Inner, and this is what reaches users in diagnostics and in introspection naming.

      Specified by:
      getCanonicalName in interface io.micronaut.inject.ast.ClassElement
